title: The 3 "K"s of Osaka Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Shinichi, Heiji, Kazuha, Ran, Kogoro, Inspector Ohtaki) omitted by convention, matching ep011. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved (person/location/object), sharing an `order` integer so edges belonging to the same occurrence can be grouped without a reifying node. The old wiki-summary-derived case file (cases/ep238-239_the_3_ks_of_osaka_case.json) got the murderer right (Ray Curtis) but misspelled both his co-owners ('Ricardo Barreira' -> actually 'Ricardo Barega') and the victim ('Ed McCay' -> actually 'Ed McKay', per the on-screen character cards), and it dropped essentially the entire case: it had no motive at all for the culprit (in the transcript, Ed McKay's tabloid story exposing Ray's drug abuse drove Ray's wife to suicide, which is why Ray killed him), no red-herring motives for the other two co-owners (Ed had also publicly exposed Ricardo's fixed fights and falsely accused Mike of an affair), and none of the physical reasoning Conan actually uses to clear Ricardo/Mike and convict Ray (the three-second timing window versus each man's assigned floor, the deflated/re-inflated soccer ball used to trigger the mechanism, the pin and wet towel found in Ray's room, the gunpowder-residue logic pointing at his shoes, and Ed's two-part dying message -- three curled fingers plus a hand on his belt -- encoding sushi-counter slang 'bandou' for the number 8, Ray's own jersey number). The trigger was a soccer ball that was kicked, not 'thrown' as the old file's object description said. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Ed McKay's dying message combines two separate signs on his body that only resolve to the same answer together: three fingers extended on his right hand (a sushi-counter hand signal Japanese staff use to discreetly convey a price/item number) and his left hand gripping his own belt ('bandou', old-fashioned Western/Japanese slang for a leather belt). Read together via the sushi-shop convention, both signs independently encode the number 8 -- the jersey number worn only by Ray Curtis.

Comparing the roughly three-second gap (from Ran's eyewitness timing) between Room #2's light and the gunshot against each owner's assigned floor and known physical condition: Ricardo (5th floor, too large/slow) and Mike (3rd-4th floor, injured arm, seen calmly opening curtains at the moment of the shot) could not have covered the distance to the crime scene in time, while Ray (1st-2nd floor, professional free-kick accuracy, knock-then-kick timing via the transceiver) could have -- and was the only one of the three who could.
